audit.whatIsWrong: 2+ items read Riven on both layers while whys[6], spikes[3] and late all say Volibear's tank scaling wins that stage. Packet chart says Volibear.
audit.why: 50.69% over 1160 games against a champion who scales into brawls; the last row contradicted its own why-text.
audit.corrected: 2+ items -> Volibear as a matched full/content pair, rating 5/10 -> 4/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[4] said Stormbringer 'adds a personal shield'. Volibear's R grants bonus Health and disables nearby enemy towers; the shield in his kit is Sky Splitter (E), gained only if he stands in his own blast.
audit.why: A player expecting a shield on R will mis-time the level 6 all-in and mis-read how much damage is needed.
audit.corrected: Stormbringer (160/135/110s, 100 mana): bonus health, slow, dash, tower disable. Sky Splitter is the shield.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three places call Sky Splitter (E) a stun — mid ('if he lands E stun during your Q-chain'), wants.you[1] ('Bait his E stun'), spikes[2] ('survive his E stun window'). Sky Splitter slows and shields; the only stun in the kit is Thundering Smash (Q). spikes[1] and wants.you[2] also treat Wind Slash as an execute with a 'second cast', and wants.you[2] told the player to sit at half HP for it.
audit.why: This is the decisive interaction of the lane inverted: players would bait the wrong ability and hold the wrong dodge, then deliberately stay low on HP for a mechanic that does not exist.
audit.corrected: Thundering Smash (12/11.5/11/10.5/10s) is the stun and an auto-attack reset — react to the wind-up. Sky Splitter is a 16s, 1200-range bolt that slows and shields him if he stands in it. Riven's R gives one Wind Slash, a ranged projectile, not an execute keyed to her own HP.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] tells the player to play around Sky Splitter's '20-second Level 1 cooldown'; the kit lists a flat 16s at every rank. It also claims Volibear has no hard CC at Level 1, which is false if he takes Q.
audit.why: A four-second error in the tracked window is exactly the gap he engages through.
audit.corrected: Sky Splitter is a flat 16s; Thundering Smash can be his level 1 pick.

audit.why: Frenzied Maul's heal is flagged in the kit and Executioner's Calling is already named in the full-layer itemization; the content layer warns to keep trades short.

edits.before: Volibear has no hard CC at Level 1 and your Q poke sets up the Level 2 all-in — identify whether he starts E and play around its 20-second Level 1 cooldown.
edits.after: Volibear has no stun unless he takes Thundering Smash first; if he opens Sky Splitter instead, it is a flat 16s bolt, so farm through it and set up your Level 2.

edits.before: His Stormbringer at 6 adds a personal shield and tower disable that shifts the dynamic — go all-in on his E cooldown with Wind Slash ready to execute, or the window closes.
edits.after: Stormbringer at 6 grants him bonus health and disables your tower — all-in on Thundering Smash's cooldown with Wind Slash held for his retreat, or the window shuts.

edits.before: Blade of the Exile extends your reach so Thundering Smash no longer lets him close the gap for free — Wind Slash executes him the moment he commits his Q dash.
edits.after: Blade of the Exile extends your reach so Thundering Smash no longer closes the gap for free — fire Wind Slash the moment he commits that Q dash toward you.

edits.before: Immortal Shieldbow's shield stacks on top of Valor to absorb his W bite burst, letting you survive his E stun window and retaliate with your full combo.
edits.after: Immortal Shieldbow stacks on top of Valor's shield to absorb his W bite, letting you eat Sky Splitter's slow and still retaliate with your full combo.

edits.before: The 4-5 window is a genuine coin flip — his Thundering Smash empowered dash keeps pressure on your dashes, and if he lands E stun during your Q-chain you lose the trade. Track his E cooldown the same way you track his Q: E is roughly 16 seconds pre-haste so you have a clear window after he burns it. At Level 6 Blade of the Exile changes the math: the extended melee range lets you land Q3 at range after the Wind Slash setup, and his Stormbringer shield does not block the execute damage of a second-cast Wind Slash at low HP. Force the all-in on his E cooldown and close it with Wind Slash if he is under 40%.
edits.after: The 4-5 window is a genuine coin flip — Thundering Smash (10-12s) is the stun, not Sky Splitter, so it is his Q that pins you mid Q-chain and it doubles as an auto reset, meaning the wind-up is your cue to step back. Sky Splitter is a flat 16s, 1200-range bolt that slows and shields him only if he stands in his own blast, so it opens trades rather than ending them. At Level 6 Blade of the Exile changes the math: the extended range lets you land Q3 from further out, and Wind Slash is one ranged projectile per R — hold it for his retreat. All-in when Thundering Smash is down, then E out before his second W bite heals him back.

edits.before: Bait his E stun before you go all-in so he has no CC to interrupt your Q3 knockup follow-up
edits.after: Bait Thundering Smash — his only stun — before you all-in, so nothing interrupts your Q3 knockup

edits.before: Stay at roughly half HP so your Wind Slash execute at 6 deals maximum damage on the commit
edits.after: Save Wind Slash for when he is low — one ranged shot per R, spend it on his escape not your opener

notes: Packet suspectNames flagged 'Thundering Smash' and 'Stormbringer' as probable wrong names; both are correct per the kit file — those are false positives, no name change made. The real defect was ability-slot confusion (Sky Splitter called a stun in three places). Full-layer prose carries mojibake em dashes on disk, so full-layer edits are limited to clean-ASCII enum fields.
